versions: Kiro spec templates: requirements.md with numbered acceptance criteria, bugfix.md with behaviour sections (2025-2026)
description: Acceptance criteria numbered by their position inside numbered requirements, bugfix criteria numbered N.M under the behaviour headings, and their citations in tasks and properties; tasks numbered 1 and 1.1 in the checkbox items of each spec's tasks.md, with their checkbox statuses.

uncertainty.text: {{items}} items of ordered lists under "{{section}}" headings inside {{keyword}} headings, in {{files}} files. Each item is a criterion numbered by its position, such as Criterion 1.2 for the second item of {{keyword}} 1.

{{citations}} citations such as "{{keyword}}s: 1.2" refer to criteria; citations of a whole {{keywordLower}} ("{{keyword}}s: 3") refer to it. A list mixing both forms stops at the first item of the other form.
It needs the {{keyword}} suggestion, or an existing {{keyword}} category.

{{count}} criteria of Kiro bugfix specifications in {{files}} files ({{sections.defect}} current, {{sections.expected}} expected, {{sections.unchanged}} unchanged behaviour) are paragraphs starting with their number, such as "2.1 The system SHALL …", which defines Criterion 2.1. They are tagged bugfix:defect, bugfix:expected, or bugfix:unchanged by their section.

tagReason.text: In {{files}} Kiro bugfix specifications, {{count}} criteria sit under the current ({{sections.defect}}), expected ({{sections.expected}}), and unchanged ({{sections.unchanged}}) behaviour headings, so they are tagged bugfix:defect, bugfix:expected, or bugfix:unchanged by their section.

uncertainty.text: {{count}} checkbox items starting with a number in {{files}} tasks.md files of Kiro specs, such as "- [ ] 1.1 Update the strategy". Each defines a task, Task 1 or Task 1.1, numbered again in each spec, so each spec is its own scope; only checkbox items in tasks.md define them, and a bare number elsewhere is not a task. Their checkboxes give their status: Done ([x]), Open ([ ]), or In progress ([-], [~], or [/]).
